title: Brinson-Fachler attribution that reconciles to the excess return
source:
"""Brinson-Fachler attribution that reconciles to the excess return exactly.

Rb = sum wb_i rb_i,  Rp = sum wp_i rp_i
allocation_i  = (wp_i - wb_i) * (rb_i - Rb)
selection_i   = wb_i * (rp_i - rb_i)
interaction_i = (wp_i - wb_i) * (rp_i - rb_i)
Summed over sectors, allocation + selection + interaction = Rp - Rb, because
sum (wp_i - wb_i) * Rb = 0 when both weight vectors sum to 1. Asserted.
"""
import os

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

INPUT = "/input/environment/data/sectors.csv"
OUT = "/app/output/attribution.csv"


def main() -> None:
    s = pd.read_csv(INPUT)
    wp, wb = s["portfolio_weight"].to_numpy(float), s["benchmark_weight"].to_numpy(float)
    rp, rb = s["portfolio_return"].to_numpy(float), s["benchmark_return"].to_numpy(float)
    Rb, Rp = float(wb @ rb), float(wp @ rp)

    allocation = (wp - wb) * (rb - Rb)
    selection = wb * (rp - rb)
    interaction = (wp - wb) * (rp - rb)
    total = allocation + selection + interaction
    assert abs(total.sum() - (Rp - Rb)) < 1e-14, "effects must reconcile to the excess return"

    out = pd.DataFrame({"sector": s["sector"], "allocation": allocation, "selection": selection,
                        "interaction": interaction, "total_effect": total})
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(OUT), exist_ok=True)
    out.to_csv(OUT, index=False, float_format="%.17g")
    back = pd.read_csv(OUT)
    assert abs(back["total_effect"].sum() - (Rp - Rb)) < 1e-12
    print(f"excess {Rp - Rb:.6f} reconciled across {len(out)} sectors")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
